# THIS FILE CARRIES NO `axisBfiled` COLUMN. The grader lifts the filed row-level axis-B value out of
# `HAND-AXES-13.tsv` itself, on (file,line,id), so no departure in P3 can come from my re-typing the
# verdict I am testing. [[feedback_slicing_the_inputs_but_retyping_the_verdict]]
# AXIS B PER CONJUNCT — the same three values as the convention's axis B, applied to the figure THIS
# conjunct reads rather than to the row:
#   immovable     no commit can change this conjunct's compared figure
#   movable       a cure to the subject moves it
#   history-keyed an anchor is a recency SELECTOR, so any commit touching the path moves it
# ANCHORKIND is the derivation the value is read THROUGH, and `evid` is the line of the subject file
# where that derivation is written, so the reading can be contested at its source rather than taken
# on my word. Four kinds appear:
#   fixed-rev      `git show <40-hex const>:<path>` — the rev is a source literal
#   rev-from-file  `rev-parse <sha>:<path>` where the sha was READ FROM A FILE at startup
#   live           `readFileSync` under `LIVE` — the worktree copy of the subject
#   run-derived    a row of this harness's OWN run table, produced by driving an arm
#   recording      a committed `.out` read from the worktree
# `state` is the PRE/POST label the subject file itself gives the operand, or `-` where the conjunct
# belongs to NEITHER state. The `-` rows are the whole reason this census can separate
# most-movable-wins from "the POST conjunct decides".

# NOTES ON THE READINGS I EXPECT TO BE CONTESTED, written here and not in RESULTS, so they are on
# the record before the grader runs:
# 1. `@194` k1..k6 are the SIX conjuncts of `ctrlPinned` (defined at :190–:193), applied to
#    `preCtrl`. My own `why` cell for this row in `HAND-AXES-13.tsv` says "five conjuncts". I count
#    six, and seven with `transition(rec3Arm)` beside them. P1 is registered to land by finding that
#    defect, not by clearing it.
# 2. `@194` k1..k6 read `movable`, not `immovable`, even though their operand is labelled PRE. The
#    PRE label there names the SOURCE STATE the arm drove, not a frozen anchor: `preCtrl` is a row
#    of this harness's own `results` table, produced by cloning the LIVE repo and running an arm in
#    it, so a cure to the subject moves the figure. This is the row that makes the census able to
#    tell most-movable-wins apart from POST-decides.
# 3. `@194` k7 reads `immovable` on the `recording` kind. A committed `.out` is not a source
#    literal — a commit COULD rewrite `drive3.steal.out`. It reads `immovable` under the clause the
#    convention actually states ("the cure's own diff does not touch the compared literal"), and it
#    is the weakest `immovable` in the table. Recorded as such rather than hardened.
# 4. `measure.mjs:79` k1/k2 are `rev-from-file`, not `fixed-rev`: the revs are shas READ AT STARTUP
#    from `sat.json` (tracked, `:48`) and `baseline.rev` (`:29`). `baseline.rev` is UNTRACKED
#    (`git ls-files --error-unmatch baseline.rev` → "did not match any file"), so no commit can move
#    MY_REV at all; `sat.json` is tracked, so HIS_REV's immovability is contingent on a file and not
#    on the source. Filed `immovable` as in `HAND-AXES-13.tsv`, with the contingency named.
# 5. The expression for `measure.mjs:79` is at `:76`, not `:79`; `:79` is the `refuse` call. That is
#    the already-published `G0@79` out-of-span finding and is not re-litigated here — the row key
#    stays `79` so this file joins to `HAND-AXES-13.tsv` on it.
# 6. `a === null || b === null` is a DISJUNCTION. "Conjunct" is used here for "top-level operand of
#    the predicate's boolean spine", which is what axis A's definition is about ("never operands of
#    ONE comparison"); the spine's operator does not change the per-operand figure. Named because a
#    reader counting `&&` alone would find zero conjuncts in this row.
